                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Merchant complaints

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Seven one-star entries inspected; six contained review text. Recurring printing and support concerns span different years.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • A March 2026 merchant reported label dimensions differing from previews and unreadable output. Two 2023 merchants described printing/template failures and difficulty reaching support. Source ↗Historical and recent allegations; current reproduction unknown.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • A 2024 merchant disputed generated GTINs. Source ↗The developer attributed this to input country/GS1 prefixes. Validate identifiers and clarify that generating a number does not establish ownership of a prefix.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Evidence gates and scoring methodology

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Opportunity = 100 × demand × new-entrant traction × buildability × exploitable weakness. Only apps passing the launch window, all three evidence gates and the weakness check receive a score. Missing evidence remains Unknown. Existing-app success is a separate historical proxy and never boosts opportunity ranking. Screening thresholds are provisional research rules, not a calibrated probability of business success.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Launch window: 24 calendar months, inclusive. Proven demand needs positive payment evidence with a period ending within 365 days; prices and free-plan reviews do not qualify. Proven entry needs comparable paying-customer or active-merchant counts over 30–90 days, ending within 30 days, with at least 5 net customers per 30 days and a documented active direct competitor older than 24 months and launched before the entrant. Reviews alone remain a proxy.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Easy build requires an explicit assessment of the core workflow, exclusions, platform access, dependencies and validation. Limits: 10 working days including quality checks, $50/month operating costs and 2 support hours/month at a stated workload. These are initial screening budgets; publishing and app-store review time are separate. Current weaknesses need at least two independent merchant reports within 180 days, a verified unresolved problem, a target segment and an improvement that fits the build scope. Competitor, build and weakness assessments expire after 90 days.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Factors: demand = 1 once payment is evidenced; entry = min(1, net customers per 30 days / 20); build = min(1, (15 − working days) / 10); weakness = min(1, independent recent merchants / 5). Opportunity = 100 × these four factors, only after every check passes. Factors and thresholds are transparent screening heuristics, not statistical probabilities. Missing factors are not renormalized. Unknown candidates form a research backlog; known failures are rejected; older apps remain comparison context.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Historical Success is a separate proxy: demand 35%, satisfaction 15%, observed review growth 20%, monetization 20%, age and Built for Shopify 10%. Missing dimensions are excluded from that historical score and shown in its coverage and bounds. It never contributes to Opportunity. Profile complexity describes a preliminary MVP hypothesis and cannot pass Easy build.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The original sample used up to 20 high-review apps from each of seven discovery pages. New research must search focused workflows and verify launch dates before selection, without a lifetime-review top-N cap. The scanner evaluates every imported app; it does not claim marketplace-wide coverage. Category totals include adjacent tools, and zero sample peers does not mean no competition. A crowded category does not automatically reduce opportunity when a young entrant demonstrates customer growth.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The price median includes only known positive monthly entry prices in USD. Annual, one-time and usage-based prices are not converted. The rating median is not weighted by review count. New apps launched within the last 30 or 90 calendar days, including the calculation date.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Developers are counted by normalized publisher name, not by individual programmers. Names can collide or change; team size requires separate evidence. The top three apps' share of category reviews is available in JSON/CSV and describes the sample, not market share.
